# Documentation home {.unnumbered #documentation-home}

This is the documentation for **Alkali Pumping v6.9.9**, a Streamlit application for modeling optical pumping and weak-RF magnetometry in alkali-vapor cells. The principal analysis is the **ACC Magnetometer**, where ACC means *antirelaxation coated cell*.

The documentation is organized by audience. It deliberately uses descriptive internal links rather than numbered chapters and equations.

## Choose a starting point {#choose-a-starting-point}

- **Operating the application:** start with [Getting started](user-manual/getting-started.qmd) and the [ACC Magnetometer workflow](user-manual/acc-magnetometer.qmd).
- **Understanding the model:** start with the [physical model overview](theory/model-overview.qmd), then follow links to optical pumping, RF response, and optical rotation.
- **Maintaining the code:** start with [software architecture](technical/software-architecture.qmd) and [solver data flow](technical/solver-data-flow.qmd).
- **Looking up a term or symbol:** use the [glossary](glossary.qmd).

## Current physical model {#current-physical-model}

The ACC Magnetometer first calculates a steady atomic state from optical pumping, electron randomization, and spin exchange. It then calculates a weak-RF density-matrix response and converts that response into atomic observables and transmitted-light Stokes signals.

When a physical pump is selected as its own probe, the configured pump intensity is used unchanged. The RF perturbation uses one [spatially uniform atomic density matrix](theory/uniform-density-matrix-feedback.qmd) driven by the path-averaged Stokes perturbation. The current solver does not create a different atomic state in every longitudinal slice.

## Documentation status {#documentation-status}

This first Quarto edition establishes the structure, terminology, main equations, operating workflow, and model limitations. The application and its automated tests remain the authority when documentation and implementation disagree; such a disagreement should be treated as a defect and corrected.
